# Same-run drawing recovery controls

Original packages generated by `tools/run_drawing_recovery_fixture.py` with
Python's standard library and the original image-recovery fixture builder.

Each fixture has mixed text/drawing runs in the body, a table cell and a header.
The runs contain supported pictures before and after an affected drawing, with
text before, between and after the pictures. Supported direct formatting and
paragraph geometry must survive throughout.

`drawing.docx` uses the currently unsupported DrawingML `alphaBiLevel` effect
on the middle drawing. `alternate.docx` places that drawing in the selected
`AlternateContent` choice, with an empty fallback. The supported `healthy.docx`
omits only the affected middle drawings. `reserved.docx` instead keeps a supported
middle picture at the same declared size. All four pass transitional schemas
after standard MCE branch selection.

Unit checks verify both retained pictures and all text/formatting in each run,
strict import rejection, read-only mode and original package preservation.
Browser comparisons check body and header geometry against the reserved-image
control, verify that the visible placeholder changes the pixels, and check
original download bytes through the UI. The placeholder screenshot is visually
reviewed. The original omission control still tests unaffected editable import.

Relevant semantics are ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.3 (run content) and 20
(DrawingML), plus Part 3 (markup compatibility branch selection). Recovery
does not implement `alphaBiLevel`, switch to another MCE branch or claim
rendering agreement with the native reference. Valid unrotated inline frames now retain their dimensions and
effect extents with a neutral missing-drawing symbol. Anchored, rotated, invalid
or oversized frames remain outside this recovery subset. The effect's actual
rendering semantics remain unsupported.
